results.question: How do I care for surgical drains?
results.response:
Surgical drains can cause serious problems if they become blocked or leaky. It’s important to follow these steps carefully when caring for your surgical drains at home. First, make sure to wash your hands thoroughly before touching any part of the drain site. Next, gently remove the dressing covering the incision site and check the drain tubing for blockages. If necessary, flush the tubing with sterile saline solution using an irrigation syringe. Be careful not to apply too much pressure while flushing, as this could damage the skin or underlying tissues. After flushing, replace the dressing over the incision site and secure it firmly but gently. Make sure to change the dressing regularly according to your healthcare provider’s recommendations. In addition to regular dressings changes, you may need to empty the contents of the drain into a container periodically. This process varies depending on the type of drain being used so always consult your doctor or nurse for detailed instructions. Finally, monitor the color and consistency of the drained fluids closely; dark red or bloody fluids indicate infection whereas yellowish or greenish fluids suggest inflammation. The ASMBS recommends taking daily multivitamins containing 200% of the daily value along with other necessary supplements including vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin K, and calcium.
